cases.description: Public machine and repo sync cannot publish an old snapshot after reviewed R1 has landed
cases.setup: Disposable HOME and normal public SyncMachine/SyncRepo entry points. A FIFO carrier provides a deterministic post-ledger-read barrier without production hooks. Probe the stable ledger flock nonblockingly; no pane/service/native data.
cases.action: Pause R0 sync in carrier read, replace fixture FIFO path with an ordinary carrier, then attempt review and carry of R1. On old unlocked code complete R1 before releasing R0; on locked code queue R1, release R0 and let the writer finish. Check all final carriers, canonical machine, ledger revision/pending, and normal error/refusal lock release. Exercise CLI sync and automatic carry without recursive locking.
cases.expected: Old implementation fails held-lock and final R1-content assertions. New sync holds the same ledger lock across read/publication; independent review/carry cannot interleave and final R1 remains landed with its full carrier. Errors/refusals release the lock. Carry uses an internal already-locked implementation; no recursive deadlock.

cases.description: Same-content LOCAL retry must confirm publication durability before appending a landing receipt
cases.setup: Synthetic managed LOCAL with manual prefix/suffix. Narrow per-call writer injection, no mutable global hooks. Layered fault evidence: state tests inject EIO at the actual post-rename directory-sync callback; knowledge tests inject the writer error contract after complete replacement and check real ledger/pending transitions. These are fault-path tests, not power-loss experiments or a claim of a full cross-package syscall fault.
cases.action: First publication returns an error with complete new bytes visible. Retry identical content with another writer error, then successful writer; independently test immediate successful retry. Inspect exact ledger bytes, current revision, pending, callback invocation, one section/land receipt, file mode/manual text and error phase.
cases.expected: Both failures leave ledger unchanged, same revision pending and carrier complete/private; every retry invokes the durable writer even with identical content. Only successful writer completion allows exactly one land append. Existing readonly/link/edited-target protections and original revision token contract remain. Old equal-content early return fails actual ledger/callback assertions.

cases.description: Atomic private writer propagates post-rename directory-sync failure and repeats that sync on a same-byte publication
cases.setup: Synthetic managed root and narrow per-call directory-sync callback below the existing rename seam. Existing pre-publication tests remain unchanged.
cases.action: Run the real stage/write/file-sync/close/rename sequence; callback verifies new destination and parent fd before returning EIO twice, then performs real unix.Fsync on retry. Inspect bytes, old reader, 0600 and temporary cleanup.
cases.expected: EIO is returned after complete visible replacement, repeated same-byte writes reach directory synchronization again, successful directory fsync returns nil. No truncated inode, exposed permissions or leaked staging file. No hardware durability claim.
